meta.name: Track IBM Quantum backend drift with Bell tests, Sheets, Gmail and OpenAI

name: Track IBM Quantum backend drift with Bell tests, Sheets and OpenAI

parameters.content:
## Quantum backend watchtower

IBM Quantum processors are recalibrated every day and their qubits drift. The pair that was the best link on the chip yesterday can be one of the worst today. This workflow measures that drift instead of guessing at it.

### How it works

The morning flow reads how much QPU time your plan has left and stops early if you are near the limit. It picks the least busy backend, downloads the live calibration report, and scores every two qubit link by CZ gate error plus the readout error of both qubits. The winning pair gets a Bell state circuit written in backend native ISA gates, so IBM accepts it without a local Qiskit transpile. The job is submitted, the run is logged as pending, and the flow ends. Nothing blocks on the queue, which can be seconds or hours.

A second trigger wakes when that job finishes, pulls the counts, finds its pending row, scores the measured correlation against what the calibration predicted, and completes the row. OpenAI reads the rolling history and writes a short assessment, delivered by Gmail as a digest or a degradation alert. A third trigger emails you when a job fails or is cancelled.

### Setup steps

1. Add IBM Quantum, Google Sheets, Gmail and OpenAI credentials.
2. Create a spreadsheet with an empty tab named `runs` and select it in all four Sheets nodes. The 25 headers are written automatically on the first run.
3. Put your address in three places: Set Watchtower Parameters, Set Alert Configuration and Alert Job Failure Report.
4. Keep `jobTag` identical in Set Watchtower Parameters and in both trigger nodes.
5. Run the morning flow once by hand, then activate.

## Schedule and budget gate

Starts the daily benchmark, applies watchtower settings, checks available QPU budget, and sends a budget-exhausted warning when there is not enough time left.

## Choose benchmark target

Selects the least busy IBM Quantum backend, reads its calibration data, and chooses the best qubit pair for the Bell benchmark.

## Validate and submit job

The circuit is already written in native rz, sx and cz gates on physical qubits. IBM does not transpile for you, so a textbook h and cx circuit comes back rejected with error 1517. That is why no local Qiskit install is needed.

## Log pending benchmark

Builds a pending-run record for the submitted quantum job and writes it to Google Sheets for later completion matching.

## Handle job failures

Listens for IBM Quantum job failures, formats the failed job details, and emails a failure alert.

## Fetch completed results

Triggers when a quantum job completes, loads alert settings, fetches the job results, and finds the corresponding pending row in Google Sheets.

## Score and save result

Calculates the Bell-test correlation score and updates the benchmark row in Google Sheets with completed results.

## Prepare drift context

Reads recent benchmark history from Google Sheets and prepares a structured drift-analysis context for the LLM.

## Summarize backend drift

Uses the LLM chain and OpenAI chat model to summarize backend drift trends from the prepared benchmark context.

## Route drift notifications

Checks whether the correlation score is below the alert threshold and sends either a degradation alert or the regular daily digest email.

parameters.jsCode:
const pair = $('Determine Optimal Qubit Pair').first().json;
const budget = $('Fetch QPU Budget').first().json;
const settings = $('Set Watchtower Parameters').first().json;
const submitted = $input.first().json;

const remaining = (budget.usage_limit_seconds == null) ? null : (budget.usage_limit_seconds - budget.usage_consumed_seconds);

function round4(v) { return (typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v)) ? Math.round(v * 10000) / 10000 : null; }
function round2(v) { return (typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v)) ? Math.round(v * 100) / 100 : null; }

return [{ json: {
  runAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  status: 'pending',
  backend: pair.backendName,
  queueLength: pair.queueLength,
  controlQubit: pair.controlQubit,
  targetQubit: pair.targetQubit,
  czError: round4(pair.czError),
  readoutErrorControl: round4(pair.readoutErrorControl),
  readoutErrorTarget: round4(pair.readoutErrorTarget),
  t1Control: round2(pair.t1Control),
  t2Control: round2(pair.t2Control),
  t1Target: round2(pair.t1Target),
  t2Target: round2(pair.t2Target),
  linksEvaluated: pair.linksEvaluated,
  calibrationUpdatedAt: pair.calibrationUpdatedAt,
  predictedCorrelation: round4(pair.predictedCorrelation),
  requestedShots: Number(settings.shots) || null,
  jobId: submitted.jobId,
  qpuSecondsRemaining: remaining,
  scoredAt: '',
  shots: '',
  correlationScore: '',
  deltaVsCalibration: '',
  antiCorrelatedShots: '',
  rawCounts: ''
} }];

parameters.content:
## Configure before the first run

Set your alert email and shots in Set Watchtower Parameters, and keep `jobTag` identical to the tag filter on both trigger nodes.

On IBM's free Open Plan the allowance is a rolling 28 day window, not a calendar month, so seconds return gradually rather than resetting on a date. A 512 shot run of this circuit costs roughly one to two QPU seconds. The budget gate stops the run whenever less than `qpuSecondsReserve` is left.
